name: Tale
description: Tale helps people and AI agents communicate project goals, expectations, boundaries, and evidence in a clear, reusable way.

definitions.name: Purpose
definitions.defaultText: Use the outcome the user requested as the goal. Restate it in plain language before substantial work and keep decisions aligned with it. Do not invent additional goals.

definitions.name: Product
definitions.defaultText:
People can save a diagram as a JSON project, reopen it, and deploy one deterministic .tale file to a chosen project. Tags and Skills are reusable notes with one editable text value each.
Keep the diagram easy to navigate with precise dragging, arrows, mouse and touchpad zoom, and clear icons. Selecting a note should show its title and one human-language text box.

definitions.name: Architecture
definitions.defaultText: Use TypeScript and Electron. Keep the application, SVG diagram editor, Electron main process, and renderer UI separate. Pass only validated data across the preload bridge.

definitions.name: Agreement
definitions.defaultText: Clarify scope and completion checks when they are genuinely unclear. Carry forward approvals already given; do not ask the user to repeat the same decision.

definitions.name: Changes
definitions.defaultText: Make the smallest reviewable change that solves the agreed problem. Deny unrelated changes. Preserve existing user work and avoid unrelated refactors, renames, or formatting sweeps.

definitions.name: Scope
definitions.defaultText: Work only in the files and behavior needed for the agreed task. Ask before expanding scope or touching an area the project marks as protected.

definitions.name: Dependencies
definitions.defaultText: Use existing project dependencies by default. Explain why a new dependency is needed and obtain the project's required approval before adding it.

definitions.name: Quality
definitions.defaultText: Follow the project's existing style and quality checks. Keep code readable and do not weaken lint, type, or formatting rules to make a change pass.

definitions.name: Testing
definitions.defaultText: Test changed behavior and relevant failure cases. Do not rewrite a passing test merely to make new code look correct; investigate a failure before changing its expectation.

definitions.name: Determinism
definitions.defaultText: When output must be reproducible, use stable ordering and formatting. Check that identical inputs produce byte-for-byte identical artifacts.

definitions.name: Deployment
definitions.defaultText: Preview the exact destination and files before deployment. Deploy only with the required authorization, preserve unrelated files, and report what changed.

definitions.name: Proof
definitions.defaultText: Report what was actually verified, including failed or skipped checks. Review the final diff against the agreed scope before saying the task is done.

definitions.name: Agentic tests
definitions.defaultText: An agent may add focused tests for its task. Do not change a passing test merely to approve a new implementation. Preserve tests once their agreed proof passes.

definitions.name: Requirement
definitions.defaultText: Treat every stated requirement as part of completion. Connect claims of success to observable behavior rather than assuming that writing code is enough.

definitions.name: Check
definitions.defaultText: Run the check that demonstrates the associated requirement. Record what was run or observed, its result, and any limitation.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Create a cross-platform Electron app for writing Tales visually. The diagram should help people organise human-language notes and relationships before sharing them with an AI agent.

items.title: Product
items.text:
People can save a diagram as a JSON project, reopen it, and deploy one deterministic .tale file to a chosen project. Tags and Skills are reusable notes with one editable text value each.
Keep the diagram easy to navigate with precise dragging, arrows, mouse and touchpad zoom, and clear icons. Selecting a note should show its title and one human-language text box.

items.title: Architecture
items.text: Use TypeScript and Electron. Keep the application, SVG diagram editor, Electron main process, and renderer UI separate. Pass only validated data across the preload bridge.

items.title: Deployment
items.text: Deploy only the generated .tale file to the selected project’s .tale directory. Keep the editor JSON outside deployment. Update the selected agent instructions without removing unrelated content..

items.title: Dependencies
items.text: Use the existing Electron, TypeScript, and Biome tools. Do not add UI or SVG libraries. Ask before adding any other dependency.

items.title: Agreement
items.text: Discuss unclear requirements and agree on scope and completion checks before editing. Respect approval already given.

items.title: Changes
items.text: Make the smallest change that solves the agreed problem. Deny unrelated changes. Ask before refactoring, renaming, moving, or deleting unrelated code.

items.title: Allowed changes
items.text: Change only the files needed for the agreed task.

items.title: Forbidden changes
items.text: Do not change .git or unrelated project files.

items.title: Approval required
items.text: Ask before changing Tale rules, agent instructions, the README, package or lock files, TypeScript configuration, or Biome configuration.

items.title: Quality
items.text: Keep TypeScript strict. Run Biome lint and formatting checks, and keep the application code readable.

items.title: Testing
items.text: Every TypeScript source file has a sibling test file. Test observable behaviour and run the relevant unit and Electron interaction checks.

items.title: Deterministic output
items.text: The same saved JSON project must generate exactly the same .tale bytes after every build. Diagram layout and colours must not change the output.

items.title: Agentic tests
items.text: An agent may add focused tests for its task. Do not change a passing test merely to approve a new implementation. Preserve tests once their agreed proof passes.

items.title: Proof
items.text: Run type checking, lint, formatting, unit tests, and Electron end-to-end tests. Review the final diff and stop when the agreed checks pass.

items.title: Deploy exact Tale bytes
items.text: Deploy the exact Tale bytes generated from the saved project JSON. Check the installed file against the compiler output.

items.title: Keep project JSON out of deployment
items.text: Keep the editor project JSON out of the destination .tale directory. Deploy only the compiled Tale.

items.title: Preserve the editor project
items.text: Deployment must leave the source project JSON unchanged.

items.title: Exercise actual deployment
items.text: Run the Electron deployment test. Confirm that the installed Tale matches the compiler output, no project JSON is installed, and the source JSON is preserved.
